newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London quiet before holiday.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London quiet before holiday.

text.p: Japanese stocks in London were steady to slightly lower in quiet afternoon trade on Friday amid limited profit-taking on Tokyo's rebound.
Dealers said activity remained modest as investors wound down for Monday's Culture Day public holiday in Japan.

In London, the Nikkei/Ise 50 index was up 4.16 points at 1,414.97. In Tokyo, the Nikkei 225 Average closed 166.20 points higher at 20,633.06, lifted by futures-related buying after a drop as low as 20,388.10.
Traders said they saw little scope for the London market to make headway next week against a stalled Tokyo bourse.

"There's still lots of uncertainty on the political front and Japan seems stuck in a fairly tight range between 20,000 and 21,000 points...we wouldn't expect any major changes to that or to low volumes," one dealer said.
"It's hard to gauge direction at the moment. The Japan market is really in wait-and-see mode and that of course has filtered down into London," a second trader said.
Traders said NEC and Mitsubishi Motors Corp eased on profit-taking.
However, Bank of Tokyo-Mitsubishi Ltd was bid higher after it revised its interim earnings forecast upwards.
Dealers said Japanese stocks would be traded in London on Monday despite the holiday in Japan but business would be thin.

"If Wall Street reacts well to the U.S. payrolls figure then we could see some follow-through in London Japanese stocks. But it's unlikely. People will wait for Tokyo to re-open," the first dealer said.
